claim: The oviduct is the site of fertilization and preimplantation embryo development in mammals.
source: The oviduct is the site of fertilization and preimplantation embryo development in mammals.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about mammalian reproduction.

claim: Gametes alter oviductal gene expression.
source: Evidence suggests that gametes alter oviductal gene expression.
evidence: Supported by citation to existing literature.

claim: The presence of sperm induces genes involved in pro-inflammatory responses in the proximal region at 0.5 days post-coitus (dpc).
source: Specifically, the presence of sperm induces genes involved in pro-inflammatory responses in the proximal region at 0.5 days post-coitus (dpc).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from bulk RNA-seq and scRNA-seq analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: Genes involved in inflammatory responses were produced specifically by secretory epithelial cells in the oviduct.
source: Genes involved in inflammatory responses were produced specifically by secretory epithelial cells in the oviduct.
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq data showing cell-type specific expression patterns.

claim: At 1.5 and 2.5 dpc, genes involved in pyruvate and glycolysis were enriched in the proximal region, potentially providing metabolic support for developing embryos.
source: At 1.5 and 2.5 dpc, genes involved in pyruvate and glycolysis were enriched in the proximal region, potentially providing metabolic support for developing embryos.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis and biological inference about metabolic support.

claim: Abundant proteins in the oviductal fluid were differentially observed between naturally fertilized and superovulated samples.
source: Abundant proteins in the oviductal fluid were differentially observed between naturally fertilized and superovulated samples.
evidence: This is supported by LC-MS/MS proteomic analysis data.

claim: The oviduct comprises four main regions: infundibulum (responsible for oocyte pick-up), ampulla (site of fertilization), isthmus (sperm capacitation/transport and preimplantation embryonic development), and the uterotubal junction (UTJ; responsible for filtering sperm and embryo transit to the uterus).
source: The oviduct comprises four main regions: infundibulum (responsible for oocyte pick-up), ampulla (site of fertilization), isthmus (sperm capacitation/transport and preimplantation embryonic development), and the uterotubal junction (UTJ; responsible for filtering sperm and embryo transit to the uterus).
evidence: This is established anatomical and functional knowledge about the oviduct.

claim: Distal (infundibulum and ampulla: IA) and proximal (isthmus and UTJ: IU) regions of the oviduct have distinct transcriptional profiles.
source: Several studies demonstrated that distal (infundibulum and ampulla: IA) and proximal (isthmus and UTJ: IU) regions of the oviduct have distinct transcriptional profiles (Roberson et al., 2021; McGlade et al., 2021; Ford et al., 2021; Harwalkar et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The presence of gametes and embryos has been shown to alter gene expression in secretory and ciliated cells of the oviduct during the preimplantation period.
source: The presence of gametes and embryos has been shown to alter gene expression in secretory and ciliated cells of the oviduct during the preimplantation period (Maillo et al., 2015; Almiñana et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2002; Fazeli et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The endometrium responded differently to in vivo-derived embryos compared to embryos derived from in vitro fertilization or somatic cell nuclear transfer in large animal models.
source: Additionally, it was reported that the endometrium responded differently to in vivo-derived embryos compared to embryos derived from in vitro fertilization or somatic cell nuclear transfer in large animal models (Mansouri-Attia et al., 2009; Bauersachs et al., 2009), suggesting a maternal response to the presence of different types of embryos.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Fertilized and unfertilized eggs with surrounding cumulus cells were in the ampulla at 0.5 dpc/dpp, respectively.
source: Fertilized and unfertilized eggs with surrounding cumulus cells were in the ampulla at 0.5 dpc/dpp, respectively (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Two-cell embryos and unfertilized eggs were clustered in the isthmus at 1.5 dpc/dpp.
source: Two-cell embryos and unfertilized eggs were clustered in the isthmus at 1.5 dpc/dpp.
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: At 2.5 dpp/dpc, unfertilized eggs and embryos at the 8-cell to the morula stage were halted in a single-file formation at the UTJ region.
source: At 2.5 dpp/dpc, unfertilized eggs and embryos at the 8-cell to the morula stage were halted in a single-file formation at the UTJ region.
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: At 3.5 dpc, the UTJ region was devoid of embryos/oocytes as all embryos/oocytes were transported to the uterus.
source: At 3.5 dpc, the UTJ region was devoid of embryos/oocytes as all embryos/oocytes were transported to the uterus and, therefore, not included in the figure.
evidence: This is supported by histological observations.

claim: IA and IU regions behave differently with respect to transcriptional activity.
source: Broad observations of region-specific transcriptome uniqueness exhibited segregation of all IA and IU biological replicates to opposite ends of the center axis on the PC1, reinforcing previous findings (Harwalkar et al., 2021) that IA and IU regions behave differently with respect to transcriptional activity.
evidence: This is supported by PCA analysis of RNA-seq data and citation to previous work.

claim: Overall transcripts at 0.5 dpc were segregated to the topmost axis along the PC2 plane, while 1.5–3.5 dpc biological replicates were segregated to the bottommost axis along the PC2 plane.
source: Surprisingly, with respect to both the IA and IU regions, overall transcripts at 0.5 dpc (Figure 1B) were segregated to the topmost axis along the PC2 plane, while 1.5–3.5 dpc biological replicates were segregated to the bottommost axis along the PC2 plane.
evidence: This is supported by PCA analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The transcriptional profile in the oviduct at all stages during the preimplantation period in the IU region is more dynamic compared to the IA region.
source: These findings indicate that oviduct transcripts from pregnant mice also possessed distinct signatures from pseudopregnant samples. Overall, data suggest that the transcriptional profile in the oviduct at all stages during the preimplantation period in the IU region is more dynamic compared to the IA region.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of DEGs between IA and IU regions across timepoints.

claim: Unique DEGs upregulated at 0.5 dpc in the IA region were enriched for the following biological processes (BPs): extracellular matrix (ECM) organization, extracellular structure organization, collagen fibril organization, and Ca2+ ion homeostasis, among others.
source: Unique DEGs upregulated at 0.5 dpc in the IA region were enriched for the following biological processes (BPs): extracellular matrix (ECM) organization, extracellular structure organization, collagen fibril organization, and Ca2+ ion homeostasis, among others (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Upregulated DEGs enriched for BPs at 0.5 dpc in the IU region included cellular response to cytokine stimulus, neutrophil migration, response to interferon-gamma, response to lipopolysaccharide, and neutrophil chemotaxis.
source: Most interestingly, we found upregulated DEGs enriched for BPs at 0.5 dpc in the IU region included cellular response to cytokine stimulus, neutrophil migration, response to interferon-gamma, response to lipopolysaccharide, and neutrophil chemotaxis (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: There are multiple BPs involved in the glucose catabolic process to pyruvate, in addition to other pyruvate metabolic processes that were uniquely upregulated at 0.5 dpc in the IU region.
source: Moreover, there are multiple BPs involved in the glucose catabolic process to pyruvate, in addition to other pyruvate metabolic processes that were uniquely upregulated at 0.5 dpc in the IU region (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: At 0.5 dpc, the sperm are present, creating a sperm reservoir in the isthmus.
source: At 0.5 dpc, the sperm are present, creating a sperm reservoir in the isthmus (Demott and Suarez, 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: When comparing 0.5 dpc to 0.5 dpp in the IU region (presence or absence of sperm, respectively), gene ontology biological processes (GOBPs) analysis revealed significant enrichment of multiple pro-inflammatory BPs, including inflammatory response, neutrophil migration, neutrophil chemotaxis, regulation of phagocytosis, positive regulation of acute inflammatory response, and response to lipopolysaccharide when sperm were present in the IU.
source: When comparing 0.5 dpc to 0.5 dpp in the IU region (presence or absence of sperm, respectively), gene ontology biological processes (GOBPs) analysis revealed significant enrichment of multiple pro-inflammatory BPs, including inflammatory response, neutrophil migration, neutrophil chemotaxis, regulation of phagocytosis, positive regulation of acute inflammatory response, and response to lipopolysaccharide when sperm were present in the IU (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E, F).
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E, F.

claim: At 0.5 dpc, the isthmus region of the oviduct was heavily regulated for an inflammatory response in the presence of sperm while simultaneously preparing for the metabolic switch of the embryos from pyruvate to glucose metabolism.
source: Therefore, it is likely that, at 0.5 dpc, the isthmus region of the oviduct was heavily regulated for an inflammatory response in the presence of sperm while simultaneously preparing for the metabolic switch of the embryos from pyruvate to glucose metabolism.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined analysis of inflammatory and metabolic pathway enrichment.

claim: Genes in the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling pathway were mostly upregulated at 0.5 dpc compared to 0.5 dpp at the IU region.
source: Next KEGG analysis was used to determine molecular players; we found that genes in the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling pathway were mostly upregulated at 0.5 dpc compared to 0.5 dpp at the IU region (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is supported by KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Most upregulated genes at 0.5 dpc were now downregulated at 1.5 dpc in the IU region.
source: Subsequently, an analysis comparing 0.5–1.5 dpc in the IU region (presence of sperm vs. presence of embryos) demonstrated the most striking results. We found that most upregulated genes at 0.5 dpc were now downregulated at 1.5 dpc (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is supported by KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The oviduct may suppress the response to inflammation in the isthmus once the sperm is cleared to become conducive for the embryo's survival at 1.5 dpc.
source: These data strongly suggest that the oviduct may suppress the response to inflammation in the isthmus once the sperm is cleared to become conducive for the embryo's survival at 1.5 dpc.
evidence: This is inferred from the temporal changes in inflammatory gene expression.

claim: All cell types previously reported were present in the oviduct.
source: First, we confirmed that all cell types previously reported (McGlade et al., 2021) were present in the oviduct (Figure 1E, F).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 1E, F and citation to previous work.

claim: There was minimum overlap between cells isolated from IA or IU regions.
source: There was minimum overlap between cells isolated from IA or IU regions (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 1G.

claim: All cell types were present at all timepoints except for an Ephx2+ cluster (only present at SO 0.5 dpc and SO estrus) and a neutrophil cluster (Ly6g+, only present at SO 0.5 dpc).
source: In addition, all cell types were present at all timepoints except for an Ephx2+ cluster (only present at SO 0.5 dpc and SO estrus) and a neutrophil cluster (Ly6g+, only present at SO 0.5 dpc).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: Genes associated with MAPK signaling pathways were mostly upregulated at SO 0.5 and SO 1.5 dpc and downregulated in SO estrus and SO 2.5 dpc in the IU regions.
source: Genes associated with these pathways were mostly upregulated at SO 0.5 and SO 1.5 dpc (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C, green and teal bars) and downregulated in SO estrus and SO 2.5 dpc in the IU regions (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D, red and purple bars).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C, D.

claim: Dusp5 was expressed at a significantly higher level at 0.5 dpc compared to 0.5 dpp.
source: We found that Dusp5 was expressed at a significantly higher level at 0.5 dpc compared to 0.5 dpp while Mapk14 (p38a) was significantly upregulated at 1.5 dpc compared to 0.5 dpc (Figure 1—figure supplement 3E, F).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR validation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3E, F.

claim: Mapk14 (p38a) was significantly upregulated at 1.5 dpc compared to 0.5 dpc.
source: We found that Dusp5 was expressed at a significantly higher level at 0.5 dpc compared to 0.5 dpp while Mapk14 (p38a) was significantly upregulated at 1.5 dpc compared to 0.5 dpc (Figure 1—figure supplement 3E, F).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR validation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3E, F.

claim: Secretory cells are the key modulators responsible for the regulation of pro- and anti-inflammatory responses during pregnancy establishment.
source: Therefore, it suggests that secretory cells are the key modulators responsible for the regulation of pro- and anti-inflammatory responses during pregnancy establishment.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of gene ontology enrichment between secretory and ciliated cells.

claim: Secreted proteins from 0.5 dpc and SO 0.5 dpc were segregated from all other timepoints.
source: In agreement with the transcriptomic data, secreted proteins from 0.5 dpc and SO 0.5 dpc were segregated from all other timepoints (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by proteomic analysis shown in Figure 2A–C.

claim: 1.5 dpc proteomic dynamics correlated more with estrus and SO estrus biological replicates, while SO 1.5 dpc correlated more with 2.5 dpc and SO 2.5 dpc.
source: Another difference was observed between 1.5 dpc and SO 1.5 dpc, at which 1.5 dpc proteomic dynamics correlated more with estrus and SO estrus biological replicates, while SO 1.5 dpc correlated more with 2.5 dpc and SO 2.5 dpc.
evidence: This is supported by proteomic analysis.

claim: There were 242 differentially abundant proteins between estrus and 0.5 dpc, 185 between 0.5 and 1.5 dpc, and 344 between 1.5 and 2.5 dpc in naturally fertilized samples.
source: Analysis comparing naturally fertilized (dpc) pregnant samples (without SO) yielded 242 differentially abundant proteins between estrus and 0.5 dpc, 185 between 0.5 and 1.5 dpc, and 344 between 1.5 and 2.5 dpc (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by proteomic analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: There were 298, 354, and 163 differentially abundant proteins when compared between SO estrus versus SO 0.5 dpc, SO 0.5 dpc versus SO 1.5 dpc, and SO 1.5 dpc versus SO 2.5 dpc, respectively.
source: There were 298, 354, and 163 differentially abundant proteins when compared between SO estrus versus SO 0.5 dpc, SO 0.5 dpc versus SO 1.5 dpc, and SO 1.5 dpc versus SO 2.5 dpc, respectively (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by proteomic analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: There were 112 differentially abundant proteins between estrus and SO estrus, 111 between 0.5 dpc and SO 0.5 dpc, 371 between 1.5 dpc and SO 1.5 dpc, and 274 between 2.5 dpc and SO 2.5 dpc.
source: In addition, protein samples from naturally fertilized and SO samples were evaluated. There were 112 differentially abundant proteins between estrus and SO estrus, 111 between 0.5 dpc and SO 0.5 dpc, 371 between 1.5 dpc and SO 1.5 dpc, and 274 between 2.5 dpc and SO 2.5 dpc (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by proteomic analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Luminal proteomics from the oviduct are dynamic during preimplantation development and SO stimulates the production and secretion of more abundant and unique proteins compared to the natural setting.
source: These results indicate that luminal proteomics from the oviduct are dynamic during preimplantation development and SO stimulates the production and secretion of more abundant and unique proteins compared to the natural setting.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of differentially abundant proteins between natural and SO conditions.

claim: A subset of shared 100 proteins were enriched for multiple pro-inflammatory Reactomes including neutrophil degranulation, innate immune system, and innate immune system.
source: We found that a subset of shared 100 proteins were enriched for multiple pro-inflammatory Reactomes including neutrophil degranulation, innate immune system, and innate immune system (Figure 2G, I).
evidence: This is supported by Reactome pathway analysis shown in Figure 2G, I.

claim: SO conditions appear to exacerbate both expression abundance and the expression of additional unique proteins with respect to pro-inflammation when compared to naturally fertilized replicates.
source: Moreover, SO conditions appear to exacerbate both expression abundance and the expression of additional unique proteins with respect to pro-inflammation when compared to naturally fertilized replicates.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of pathway enrichment between natural and SO conditions.

claim: There was a significant induction of Tlr2 at 0.5 dpc compared to 0.5 dpp at the isthmus and UTJ regions.
source: We found a significant induction of Tlr2 at 0.5 dpc compared to 0.5 dpp at the isthmus and UTJ regions (Figure 3A, B).
evidence: This is supported by RNAScope in situ hybridization staining shown in Figure 3A, B.

claim: Ptprc+ and Ly6g+ signals aggregated with greater intensities in the mesosalpinx, stromal layer, and blood vessels in the oviduct.
source: Ptprc+ and Ly6g+ signals aggregated with greater intensities in the mesosalpinx, stromal layer, and blood vessels in the oviduct.
evidence: This is supported by RNAScope in situ hybridization staining.

claim: No positive Ly6g+ cell expression was found in the luminal space of the oviduct, but rather restricted to stromal and epithelial cell linings along with blood vessels.
source: Additionally, no positive Ly6g+ cell expression was found in the luminal space of the oviduct, but rather restricted to stromal and epithelial cell linings along with blood vessels.
evidence: This is supported by RNAScope in situ hybridization staining.

claim: The relative fluorescent signal of NFκB was significantly greater at 0.5 dpc compared to 1.5 dpc or 0.5 dpp.
source: The relative fluorescent signal was significantly greater at 0.5 dpc compared to 1.5 dpc or 0.5 dpp (Figure 3C, D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescent staining shown in Figure 3C, D.

claim: p-p38:total p38 ratio was significantly increased at 0.5 dpp compared to 0.5 dpc.
source: Specifically, p-p38:total p38 ratio was significantly increased at 0.5 dpp compared to 0.5 dpc, suggesting an overall inflammatory response induced by mating regardless of the sperm exposure.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting analysis.

claim: An overall inflammatory response is induced by mating regardless of the sperm exposure.
source: Specifically, p-p38:total p38 ratio was significantly increased at 0.5 dpp compared to 0.5 dpc, suggesting an overall inflammatory response induced by mating regardless of the sperm exposure.
evidence: This is inferred from the p38 phosphorylation data.

claim: There was no difference in IL1β levels between timepoints.
source: However, there was no difference in IL1β levels between timepoints (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: An innate immune response occurs at 0.5 dpc in the isthmus and UTJ regions.
source: To summarize, these data suggest that an innate immune response occurs at 0.5 dpc in the isthmus and UTJ regions and that some of these responses were induced by the presence of seminal plasma regardless of the sperm.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined analysis of multiple markers.

claim: Some of the innate immune responses at 0.5 dpc were induced by the presence of seminal plasma regardless of the sperm.
source: To summarize, these data suggest that an innate immune response occurs at 0.5 dpc in the isthmus and UTJ regions and that some of these responses were induced by the presence of seminal plasma regardless of the sperm.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison between dpc and dpp samples.

claim: The integrative transformer model was effective in predicting the protein abundance levels from bulk RNA-seq expression data with high accuracy.
source: The integrative transformer model was effective in predicting the protein abundance levels from bulk RNA-seq expression data with high accuracy.
evidence: This is supported by the evaluation of the machine learning model.

claim: The predictive model suggests that ITs and IPs present at 0.5 dpc indicate a pro-inflammatory condition, followed by a shift to ciliogenesis and cellular stress maintenance at 1.5 dpc, subsequently initiating cellular homeostasis at 2.5 dpc.
source: Moreover, the predictive model suggests that ITs and IPs present at 0.5 dpc indicate a pro-inflammatory condition, followed by a shift to ciliogenesis and cellular stress maintenance at 1.5 dpc, subsequently initiating cellular homeostasis at 2.5 dpc.
evidence: This is inferred from the machine learning model predictions.

claim: Some of the sperm-induced inflammatory genes identified from the mouse study were present and upregulated in hydrosalpinx samples compared to healthy subjects.
source: We found that some of the sperm-induced inflammatory genes identified from our mouse study were present and upregulated in hydrosalpinx samples compared to healthy subjects (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by reanalysis of publicly available scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The differentially expressed levels of CCL3 appeared to be marginal between healthy versus hydrosalpinx samples.
source: However, the differentially expressed levels, for example the CCL3 gene, appeared to be marginal between healthy versus hydrosalpinx samples (Figure 5B, C and Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B, C.

claim: The top five most enriched GOBPs related to inflammatory responses in hydrosalpinx were Regulation of Complement Activation, Positive Regulation of Macrophage Migration Inhibitory Factor Signaling Pathway, MHC Class II Protein Complex Assembly, Positive Regulation of NK Cell Chemotaxis, and Negative Regulation of Metallopeptidase Activity.
source: Nevertheless, the top five most enriched GOBPs related to inflammatory responses were Regulation of Complement Activation, Positive Regulation of Macrophage Migration Inhibitory Factor Signaling Pathway, MHC Class II Protein Complex Assembly, Positive Regulation of NK Cell Chemotaxis, and Negative Regulation of Metallopeptidase Activity (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: GOBPs in hydrosalpinx differed from those identified in sperm-exposed mouse oviducts at 0.5 dpc, which were enriched for neutrophil-related pathways, unlike macrophages or NK cells in hydrosalpinx samples.
source: These GOBPs differed from those identified in sperm-exposed mouse oviducts at 0.5 dpc, which were enriched for neutrophil-related pathways, unlike macrophages or NK cells in hydrosalpinx samples.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of gene ontology enrichment between mouse and human samples.

claim: Sperm were likely the key mediators in modulating inflammatory responses in the oviduct, potentially priming the oviduct to become tolerable to the presence of embryos.
source: Most novel findings from this study suggest that: (1) sperm were likely the key mediators in modulating inflammatory responses in the oviduct, potentially priming the oviduct to become tolerable to the presence of embryos
evidence: This is inferred from the combined analysis of transcriptomic and proteomic data.

claim: The oviduct is an immuno-dynamic organ, alternating between a pro-inflammatory condition at 0.5 dpc to seemingly prioritizing epithelial barrier integrity/rejuvenation and cellular homeostasis between 1.5 and 2.5 dpc.
source: (3) the oviduct is an immuno-dynamic organ, alternating between a pro-inflammatory condition at 0.5 dpc to seemingly prioritizing epithelial barrier integrity/rejuvenation and cellular homeostasis between 1.5 and 2.5 dpc
evidence: This is inferred from the temporal changes in gene expression and protein abundance.

claim: The oviduct could provide necessary nutrient enrichment in the luminal fluid at different stages of embryonic development.
source: (4) the oviduct could provide necessary nutrient enrichment in the luminal fluid at different stages of embryonic development.
evidence: This is inferred from the enrichment of metabolic pathways at different timepoints.

claim: Ciliated epithelial cells in the ampulla region are responsible for creating a circular motion of the cumulus–oocyte complexes (COCs) within the ampulla.
source: Wang and Larina showed that during this timepoint, ciliated epithelial cells in the ampulla region are responsible for creating a circular motion of the cumulus–oocyte complexes (COCs) within the ampulla (Wang and Larina, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: When the COCs are present in the ampulla, ciliated cells are functionally active.
source: Here, using scRNA-seq analysis, we found that the ciliated cell population showed suppressed expression of genes involved in cilia assembly at SO 0.5 dpc and in SO Estrus (COCs are present in these two groups) in the IA region. This finding suggests that when the COCs are present in the ampulla, ciliated cells are functionally active.
evidence: This is inferred from the scRNA-seq analysis of ciliated cell gene expression.

claim: SO increases the number of mature follicles, ovulated eggs, and follicular fluid.
source: As SO increases the number of mature follicles (therefore, estrogen levels), ovulated eggs, and follicular fluid, it is also likely that these biological alterations could lead to changes in the protein abundance in the oviduct.
evidence: This is established knowledge about superovulation effects.

claim: DUSP proteins modulate inflammation and antimicrobial immune responses.
source: DUSP proteins modulate inflammation and antimicrobial immune responses (Arthur and Ley, 2013), and MAPK signaling pathways are involved in both pro- and anti-inflammatory pathways (Arthur and Ley, 2013; Kaminska, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: MAPK signaling pathways are involved in both pro- and anti-inflammatory pathways.
source: DUSP proteins modulate inflammation and antimicrobial immune responses (Arthur and Ley, 2013), and MAPK signaling pathways are involved in both pro- and anti-inflammatory pathways (Arthur and Ley, 2013; Kaminska, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The observed inflammatory response was facilitated in part by the activation of MAPK signaling pathways, as indicated by a significant increase in expression of Dusp5, which was unique to the IU region after sperm exposure.
source: Therefore, we hypothesized that the observed inflammatory response was facilitated in part by the activation of MAPK signaling pathways, as indicated by a significant increase in expression of Dusp5, which was unique to the IU region after sperm exposure.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined analysis of MAPK pathway genes and Dusp5 expression.

claim: The presence of sperm at 0.5 dpc induces a strong pro-inflammatory response in the IU region with upregulation of genes involved in inflammatory cytokines, neutrophil activation, lymphocyte recruitment, and T-cell proliferation.
source: Overall, the presence of sperm at 0.5 dpc induces a strong pro-inflammatory response in the IU region with upregulation of genes involved in inflammatory cytokines, neutrophil activation, lymphocyte recruitment, and T-cell proliferation.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined analysis of multiple inflammatory pathways.

claim: The oviduct is immunodynamic as indicated by the presence of immune cells such as neutrophils (Ly6g+), leukocyte (Ptrpc+), T cells (Cd3d+, Cd3g+), NK cells (Nkg7+, Klrb1c+), among others.
source: scRNA-seq data suggest that the oviduct is immunodynamic as indicated by the presence of immune cells as indicated by several immune markers such as neutrophils (Ly6g+), leukocyte (Ptrpc+), T cells (Cd3d+, Cd3g+), NK cells (Nkg7+, Klrb1c+), among others.
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: Sperm migration from the uterus through the UTJ into the oviduct has been an observable phenomenon dating back five decades.
source: Sperm migration from the uterus through the UTJ into the oviduct has been an observable phenomenon dating back five decades (Krzanowska, 1974).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Phagocytic bodies engulfing sperm in mice luminal fluid in the isthmus region have been observed in literature pre-dating the 1980s.
source: Additionally, phagocytic bodies engulfing sperm in mice luminal fluid in the isthmus region have also been observed in literature pre-dating the 1980s (Chakraborty and Nelson, 1975).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: 'Fit' sperm display inherently, via intracellular processes and genetic cargos, membrane 'passport' proteins that allow them to not only gain access through the UTJ, but also subsequently bind to the epithelium in the isthmus region.
source: The prevailing theory is that 'fit' sperm display inherently, via intracellular processes and genetic cargos, membrane 'passport' proteins that allow them to not only gain access through the UTJ, but also subsequently bind to the epithelium in the isthmus region (Xiong et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Sperm must evade phagocytosis from an innate immune response.
source: The in situ hybridization analysis of the IU region reinforces these observations, suggesting additionally that not only do sperm require specific membrane proteins to function properly in the uterus and oviduct, but also that sperm must evade phagocytosis from an innate immune response.
evidence: This is inferred from the in situ hybridization analysis.

claim: Ptrprc+ cells were present in the stromal and epithelial layers in the presence of sperm at 0.5 dpc in the UTJ.
source: Our findings showed that Ptrprc+ cells were present in the stromal and epithelial layers in the presence of sperm at 0.5 dpc in the UTJ.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization analysis.

claim: A significant increase in Tlr2+ cells was observed at the epithelial lining of the isthmus and UTJ regions.
source: Similarly, a significant increase in Tlr2+ cells was observed at the epithelial lining of the isthmus and UTJ regions.
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization analysis.

claim: Tlr2 is a part of the Toll-like receptor superfamily of proteins that participate in and modulate immune responses.
source: Tlr2 is a part of the Toll-like receptor superfamily of proteins that participate in and modulate immune responses (Oliveira-Nascimento et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Tlr2 has an additional role in facilitating epithelial cell barrier integrity and remodeling after a significant immune response has occurred.
source: Previous and ongoing studies suggest an additional role for Tlr2 in facilitating epithelial cell barrier integrity and remodeling after a significant immune response has occurred (Abreu, 2010; Al Sadi et al., 2021a; Al Sadi et al., 2021b; Rakoff-Nahoum et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Tlr2 expression increased at 0.5 dpc in response to the presence of sperm that may modulate epithelial cell integrity, thereafter, inducing remodeling in damaged cells at 1.5 and 2.5 dpc.
source: As such, we suggest a model where Tlr2 expression increased at 0.5 dpc in response to the presence of sperm that may modulate epithelial cell integrity, thereafter, inducing remodeling in damaged cells at 1.5 and 2.5 dpc.
evidence: This is a speculative model based on the observed Tlr2 expression pattern.

claim: An increase in NFκB fluorescent signal at 0.5 dpc indicates conditions favorable for pro-inflammation.
source: We observed an increase in NFκB fluorescent signal at 0.5 dpc, indicating conditions favorable for pro-inflammation.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescent staining analysis.

claim: Sperm have the capacity to induce immune-related responses in the uterus and oviduct.
source: Previous work both in vivo and in vitro in the uterus and oviduct, respectively, indicate sperm have the capacity to induce immune-related responses (Yousef et al., 2016; Marey et al., 2020; Schjenken et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The uterus provides a hostile, phagocytic environment to remove excessive and dead sperm.
source: In the uterus, observations suggest a hostile, phagocytic environment to remove excessive and dead sperm (Marey et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The oviduct provides an equally hostile response to allogenic sperm at 0.5 dpc.
